# PitBoard reference

Every reading the row and its cards show, the levels that colour them, the environment variables and
files PitBoard reads, and what it needs to run. The tables come from the plugin's code: `python
.ci/docs_facts.py build` writes its facts, and `python .ci/pages.py build` writes the tables from
them.

The list shows every label the row and its cards can show, in alphabetical order. A model-scoped
weekly limit takes the model's name as its label, such as `Fable`, so its label depends on the
account and is not in the list.

### The row

The row has four groups of readings: context, cache, the five-hour limit, and the week (the Part
block, `7d`, and a model-scoped limit while it needs attention), parted by `│` in the CLI and by a
thin rule in Desktop. Readings of one group are parted by a dot. `ⓘ` closes the row; in the CLI a `[
PitBoard ]` button follows it, and after that the buttons other plugins add, parted by `|`. In
Desktop the buttons are not in the row; they sit in the footer.

| Reading | CLI | Desktop |
|---|---|---|
| `Ctx` | Two-cell gauge; `↻` after it while auto-compact is on, then `ᶻ` while idle compaction is expected; the percentage once it leaves calm | Pie; a drawn circular double arrow while auto-compact is on, then a drawn pair of z letters (the sleep sign) while idle compaction is expected; the percentage once it leaves calm |
| `Cache` | Two-cell gauge that fills as the cache's time to live (TTL) runs out; a flame while a reply runs; a snowflake once the cache has expired; the countdown once it leaves calm | Pie, flame, or snowflake, as in the CLI; the countdown once it leaves calm |
| `Hit` | Not in the row: the `Cache` card carries `Hit, last turn` and `Hit, session`, and the `/pitboard` pane's Cache card keeps them too | The same |
| `5h`, `7d` | Two-cell gauge; the percentage once it leaves calm | Bar with a tick (the share of the window gone) and a paler forecast at the reset, the percentage and the time to reset at every level; see [Desktop limit styles](#desktop-limit-styles) |
| `☼` `☾` | Two-cell gauge and `<spent>/<share>`, in points of the week, before `7d`; `☼` for a working-hours part, `☾` for off-hours; only while PaceLine's week plan is usable and the part has a share, or at least 1 point was spent in a part without one | Bar and `<spent>/<share>`, with a tick at the share of the part's time gone and a paler forecast at its end |
| Model-scoped limit (`Fable`, ...), after `7d`, only while it is amber or red; a calm one is in the `/pitboard` pane | Two-cell gauge; the percentage once it leaves calm | Pie; the percentage once it leaves calm |
| Advisor | Its own group between `Ctx` and `Cache`, only while an advisor is set; a click opens its line; also in the `ⓘ` line | Its own group between `Ctx` and `Cache`, only while an advisor is set |
| Branch | In the `ⓘ` line | In the session card |
| `ⓘ` | Opens the session line | Shows the session card |
| `PitBoard` | A button, `[ PitBoard ]`, beside `ⓘ`; opens the `/pitboard` pane and closes it on the next click | A button, `[ PitBoard ]`, in the footer under the prompt, between the mode and the model name, outside the row; opens the `/pitboard` pane and closes it on the next click |
| Another plugin's button, for example `PaceLine` (`[ PaceLine ]` in the CLI, `[ PaceLine ]` in Desktop) | After `[ PitBoard ]`, parted from it by `\|`; added by that plugin, see [Buttons of other plugins](#buttons-of-other-plugins) | In the footer after the `[ PitBoard ]` button, as its own `[ <label> ]` button with no `\|` between them; not in the row |

A CLI gauge is two cells of a block that rises in eighths over a grey track, in the level's colour
once the reading leaves calm. A Desktop pie or bar fills in the same colours.

In the CLI, a click on a reading's name, or Enter while the name has focus, opens its card as one
line under the row, with `▲` under the opened name and a line of advice when the reading needs a
decision. A second click closes it. In Desktop, pointing at a reading shades it and shows its card.

### Buttons of other plugins

Another plugin can add its own button after PitBoard's, in the CLI row and in the Desktop footer.
Its hooks module calls `$.pitboard.addButton({ key, label })`, typically at session start, and
answers the press itself: PitBoard draws the button keyed `button-<key>`, and a press reaches the
adding plugin's `ui.press` hook that matches `{ plugin: 'pitboard', element: 'button-<key>' }`.
PaceLine adds its `PaceLine` button this way: `[ PaceLine ]` in the CLI, `[ PaceLine ]` in Desktop.

```
await $.pitboard.addButton({ key: 'paceline', label: 'PaceLine' })
on('ui.press', { plugin: 'pitboard', element: 'button-paceline' }, async ($, e, next) => { /* ... */ return next(e) })
```

In the CLI row PitBoard draws `|` between buttons and nowhere else; in Desktop each button is its
own chip in the footer, read `[ <label> ]`, with no `|`. Buttons come in the order they were added.
A key is a lowercase letter followed by up to 31 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens; a label is 1
to 16 printable ASCII characters after trimming. Adding a key again replaces its label. PitBoard
takes at most two buttons; a third key, a bad key or a bad label is refused and the call rejects.
Where PitBoard is not installed, `$.pitboard` is missing and the call throws, so a plugin makes the
call in a `try`.

### Desktop limit styles

PitBoard tries to keep the Desktop row on one line. It estimates the row's width character by
character and picks the fullest style that fits the window with 1.5 cells to spare. Before it drops
from Bars to Bars without reset, it tries Bars without `ⓘ`. The estimate can still be off by about a
third of a cell (see [The Desktop row can wrap within about a third of a
cell](limitations.md#the-desktop-row-can-wrap-within-about-a-third-of-a-cell)):

| Style | `5h` and `7d` drawn as |
|---|---|
| Bars | A bar with the percentage and the time to reset |
| Bars without reset | A bar with the percentage; the card still shows the time to reset |
| Pies | A pie, as the other readings; the percentage and time to reset only once the limit leaves calm |

### Cards

| Card | Rows |
|---|---|
| Context | Auto-compact, Used, Left, Window, Turns left |
| Cache | Countdown, TTL, If cold |
| Cache hits | Last turn, Session |
| 5h limit | Used, Resets in, Pace, Budget, At reset, Runs out or Threshold, Account |
| Week | Used, Resets, Pace, Week elapsed, Runs out or At reset, Forecast, Account |
| Part | Hours, Share, Spent, Spare or Overspent, Budget, Pace, At part end, Forecast, Mode, Reserve |
| A model-scoped limit, titled by the model's name | Used, Resets, Account |
| Advisor | Model, Main, State |
| `ⓘ`, titled by the main model's name | Effort, Advisor, Claude Code, Started in, Branch, Running, Turns, API cost |

- Context: `Auto-compact` reads `on` or `off`. When a smaller compaction window is set, it adds who
  set it: `env`, `settings`, `account`, `experiment`, `model default`, or `default`. `Used` counts
  toward the compaction point while auto-compact is on, and toward the full window while it is off.
  `Left` shows only while the compaction point is below the full window. `Window` shows only while
  auto-compact is on, as `<compaction window> of <model window>` when the two differ. The compaction
  point is read again as soon as `/autocompact`, `/model` or `/config` finishes. `Turns left` shows
  while auto-compact is on, once the context has grown over at least two of the last turns.
- Cache: `Countdown` reads whole minutes while calm, `mm:ss` once it warns, `replying` while a reply
  runs, and `expired` after the cache has expired. `TTL` reads `1h` or `5m`, or `5m?` until a cache
  write has shown which; in a new session that takes a few seconds after the first reply. `If cold`
  is the context the next turn writes again, and how many times dearer that turn is than a warm one
  for the session's model, such as `~40×`; `≥20×` marks a model whose cache-read price PitBoard does
  not know, so the ratio is a lower bound.
- Cache hits: both rows are cache reads divided by reads plus writes. `Session` counts from the last
  compaction.
- 5h limit, Week and a model-scoped limit: `Account` shows only as `unknown`, when a figure of the
  limit comes from the limits file and the file cannot be told to be the signed-in account's: the
  account could not be resolved, or the figures come from readings with no account. Figures from the
  session's own reply are never marked.
- 5h limit: `At reset` gives the projected percentage at the reset. `Runs out` replaces it with the
  clock time the limit reaches 100% when that comes before the reset. With PaceLine's projection,
  `Threshold` takes the place of `Runs out`: it gives the threshold and the clock time the limit
  reaches it, for example `95% at 19:40` (the threshold is 95% by default, in working hours and
  off-hours alike), and `Budget` is the pace that reaches that threshold at the reset. See [Budget,
  At reset, Runs out](explanation.md#budget-at-reset-runs-out).
- Week: `Pace` is the average rate since the weekly reset, `Week elapsed` the share of the week
  gone, and `At reset` the percentage the week reaches at that rate, or `Runs out` the time it
  reaches 100% when that comes first. From the first hour of the week; before it, `Forecast` gives
  the time it starts. A `≈` before a figure marks a forecast resting on under 48 hours of the week.
  `Used` reads `<1%` while under 1 point was spent, and `~` with one decimal when the rate puts the
  week a little past the whole percent. `Spare` and `Overspent` are on the Part card.
- Part: shown while PaceLine's week plan is usable and the current part has a share, or at least 1
  point of the week was spent in a part without one. `Hours` reads `work` or `off` and the part's
  start and end; `Share` reads the part's points, or `none (not planned)`. `Spent` reads `<1` under
  one point, and a `~` marks an estimate from the part's own rate. `Spare` or `Overspent` is the
  distance from the share pro rata by now, in points and in hours of the part's rate. `Budget` is
  what is left of the share over the hours left; `Pace` is the part's average since its start, read
  as a bound (`<`) under one point, and `At part end` is where that pace lands; both from 15 minutes
  into the part, and before that `Forecast` gives the time they start. `Mode` reads `inform` or
  `limit`, and `Reserve` reads the kept percent and its release (`8% until Fri 09:00`, `8% to the
  reset`, `8% released Fri 09:00`), or `unknown: the stop is off` when the release cannot be told,
  and is left out when the reserve is 0. In the row's short card `Mode` shows only in `limit` mode
  and `Reserve` only while its stop holds. Without PaceLine's week plan file there is no Part block.
  [Colours](explanation.md#colours) gives the rule.
- `ⓘ`: `Branch` shows only when the branch could be read; see [The Branch row is
  missing](troubleshooting.md#the-branch-row-is-missing). `API cost` is the session at API prices; a
  subscription is not charged per token. The pane's Session card, and only that card, starts with an
  `Account` row holding the signed-in account's e-mail address when it is known: from
  `CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL` in a Desktop session, else from `oauthAccount.emailAddress` in
  `.claude.json`. The row, its `ⓘ` card and the CLI detail line do not show it.
- A row reads `n/a` while its number is unknown, for example `Pace` before it has enough readings.

The Desktop card shows the rows, the bar of a limit, and advice when the reading needs a decision.
In the row the cards are short: the reset joins the title (`5h limit · resets in 2h 10m`, `Week ·
resets Fri 09:00`), the Part card's hours join its title, `Pace` reads `3.2 of 4.1%/h`, and the
Cache card adds `Hit, last turn` and `Hit, session`. The pane keeps every row. While the `/pitboard`
pane is open, the Desktop row shows no cards. The `/pitboard` pane, which either `PitBoard` button
also opens, opens with a verdict and a Next list, then folds every card into one line under
`Limits`, `This conversation` and `Session`, in the row's order; pressing a line unfolds all the
card's rows, its advice and, one press further, its explanations. The Cache card carries the `Hit`
rows. See [Open every card with `/pitboard`](how-to.md#open-every-card-with-pitboard), and the pane
itself in the CLI and in Desktop in [Getting started, step
3](https://agentpit-lab.github.io/agentpit/plugins/pitboard/docs/getting-started.html#install).

## Levels

Where each reading turns amber (watch) and red (act):

| Reading | Level | Starts at (below, for minutes left) |
|---|---|---|
| cache_1h_minutes_left | watch | 15 |
| cache_1h_minutes_left | act | 5 |
| cache_5m_minutes_left | watch | 2.5 |
| cache_5m_minutes_left | act | 1 |
| context_pct | watch | 60 |
| context_pct | act | 80 |
| five_hour_pct | watch | 70 |
| five_hour_pct | act | 90 |
| week_pct | watch | 80 |
| week_pct | act | 95 |

A reading is calm (grey), watch (amber), or act (red). The table gives the value where each level
starts: a percentage for context and limits, and minutes left for the cache, where the level starts
below the value. `context_pct` is `Ctx`, `five_hour_pct` is `5h`, `week_pct` is `7d` and every
model-scoped limit, and `cache_1h_minutes_left` and `cache_5m_minutes_left` are `Cache` with a
one-hour and a five-minute TTL.

- Context also turns act at three turns left or fewer, while auto-compact is on.
- The five-hour limit also turns act when its Pace is above its Budget, because at that pace it runs
  out before the reset. With PaceLine's projection, it turns act when PaceLine reports that the
  window would reach its threshold before the reset and its limit data is at most 30 minutes old.
  PitBoard reads the burn file only while it is at most 3 minutes old; an older file is ignored. See
  [Colours](explanation.md#colours).
- The weekly limit and each model-scoped limit use the same levels, from the percentage used only.
  With PaceLine's week plan, the week's gauge on the row and the Week card's title take the highest
  level of the percentage, the part against its share (amber above it in `inform` mode, red in
  `limit` mode) and `Reserve`; the Part gauge takes the plan's and the reserve's levels. A
  model-scoped limit is in the row only while it is amber or red.
- The cache levels follow from the TTL: watch below the lesser of 15 minutes and half the TTL, act
  below the lesser of 5 minutes and a fifth of the TTL. The countdown ends 5 seconds before the TTL.
- An expired cache is blue in Desktop and teal in the terminal, apart from the levels.
- `Hit, last turn` and `Hit, session` (in the Cache card in the pane) and the Session card have no
  levels.

Inside the cards, some rows have colours of their own:

| Row | Colour |
|---|---|
| 5h `Pace` above `Budget` | Red |
| 5h `At reset` at 80% or more | Amber |
| 5h and Week `Runs out` | Red |
| 5h `Threshold` | Red |
| Part `Pace` above `Budget`, and Part `At part end` above the share | Amber |
| Week `At reset` at 80% or more | Amber |
| Advisor `State` `inactive`, `ⓘ` `Advisor` when inactive | Amber |
| Context `Auto-compact` `on` | Green |
| Part `Overspent`, while the part is above its share | Amber in `inform` mode, red in `limit` mode |
| Week `Reserve`, from 100 minus the reserve until the release | Red |

## Environment variables

| Variable | Use |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | The Claude Code configuration directory; `~/.claude` when unset. |
| `USERPROFILE`, `HOME` | The home directory for `~/.claude`, `USERPROFILE` first. |
| `PACELINE_STATE_DIR` | PaceLine's state directory, where the limits file lies. |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ACCOUNT_UUID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ORGANIZATION_UUID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL` | The signed-in account, which the Claude Code Desktop host passes to its session. When both are set and the account variable is a UUID, the row shows that account's partition of the limits file; otherwise the account comes from `.claude.json`. `CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL` is the account's e-mail address, which the host passes with them; the pane's Session card shows it. |
| `LC_ALL`, `LC_TIME`, `LANG` | The locale for weekday names, read in this order on every OS; `C` and `POSIX` are skipped. When none gives a locale, PitBoard asks `pwsh`. |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS` | The context size from which idle compaction applies, for the Idle compact row. Claude Code's minimum is 100,000 and its default 200,000; a positive whole number below 100,000 counts as 100,000, and any other value gives the default. |
| `DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT` | When set to `1`, `true`, `yes` or `on`, auto-compact and idle compaction are off, and the Idle compact row reads off. |
| `PITBOARD_SCENARIO` | For plugin development: draws the pane from a scenario file (a JSON `ViewInput` with a fixed time) instead of live readings. Unset in normal use; it reads nothing and writes nothing. |

PitBoard reads these variables from the environment Claude Code started in.

## Files read

`<config>` is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude`. `<state>` is `$PACELINE_STATE_DIR` when it is
set and not empty, else `<config>/state/paceline`, the rule PaceLine uses.

| File | What PitBoard takes from it | When |
|---|---|---|
| `<config>/settings.json` | `advisorModel`; the effort level for `/effort` | At session start, after each turn, every 20 seconds, and after `/advisor` and `/effort` |
| `<state>/rate-limits.json` | Five-hour and weekly readings and model-scoped limits, from the partition of the signed-in account | At session start, after each turn, and every 20 seconds |
| `<state>/rate-limits.history.jsonl` and its rotated `.1` | Earlier readings of the signed-in account, for Pace | At session start |
| `<config>/.claude.json`, else `~/.claude.json` | The signed-in account, as a 16-hex-digit SHA-256 key of `oauthAccount.accountUuid` and `organizationUuid`; and `oauthAccount.emailAddress`, held in memory for the pane's Session card; nothing else in the file | With the limits file |
| `<state>/five-hour-burn-<key>.json` | PaceLine's projection of the five-hour limit to its threshold: the account, window and percentage it was computed for, the rate, the budget rate, the threshold and the time it is reached, and whether the burn is limited | With the limits file |
| `<state>/week-plan-<key>.json` | PaceLine's week plan: the current part with its share, the mode, the reserve and the later parts | With the limits file, for the signed-in account's key only |
| `<state>/last-request-<key>.json` | The time of the account's newest request, for the signed-in account's key only: whether anything was spent in a period that began after the last whole-percent step | With the limits file |
| `<config>/projects/<start directory>/<session id>.jsonl` | Cache reads and writes since the last compaction; the TTL; the last request's time | At session start, after each turn, and after `/clear` or a resume |

- The limits file and its history are PaceLine's; [PaceLine's
  reference](../../paceline/docs/reference.md#the-limits-file-for-readers) describes their format.
  PitBoard keeps the key of the account and the samples it stores together, and drops stored samples
  that belong to another account.
- `.claude.json` is Claude Code's own file, in `<config>` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set, else in
  the home directory itself, never in `~/.claude`. PitBoard reads it, never writes it, and keeps
  only the key.
- The transcript folder is the start directory with every character other than a letter or digit
  turned into `-`. When the transcript is not there, PitBoard searches every folder under
  `<config>/projects`.
- Claude Code reads a file of up to 4 MiB for a plugin. For a longer transcript, PitBoard reads its
  last 4 MB through `node`.
- Until the first request reports an effort level, the effort comes from `modelSettings` or
  `effortLevel` in the settings Claude Code loaded.
- The burn file is PaceLine's too: PitBoard reads `five-hour-burn-<key>.json` for the signed-in
  account's key and no other burn file. A key that cannot be read for a moment keeps the last one,
  and with no key at all no file is read. [Its
  format](../../paceline/docs/reference.md#the-five-hour-burn-file-for-readers) is the contract.
  PitBoard uses a file for the `5h limit` card only while it is at most 3 minutes old and matches
  the signed-in account, the window and the percentage on the row. A missing or unreadable file
  draws the row from PitBoard's own readings. The week plan file, `week-plan-<key>.json`, is read
  the same way, except that a read that fails for a moment keeps the last plan, and a file that
  cannot be parsed drops it: PitBoard reads it for the signed-in account's key only, and [its
  format](../../paceline/docs/reference.md#the-week-plan-file-for-readers) is the contract. The Week
  card uses it only while the file belongs to the signed-in account and the week on the card, and
  its current part holds the present time; otherwise the card is the even-pace card. The
  last-request file, `last-request-<key>.json`, is read the same way for the signed-in account's
  key; [its format](../../paceline/docs/reference.md#the-last-request-file-for-readers) is the
  contract. PitBoard uses it only for version 1, the same account and a time that parses, keeps the
  newest time seen and forgets it when the account changes. It also notes the time of its own
  session's requests in memory, so without PaceLine the `<1` figures rest on those and on the
  five-hour readings.

PitBoard runs these processes, in the CLI and in Desktop:

| Command | For |
|---|---|
| `git branch --show-current`, in the start directory | `Branch`, at session start and after each turn |
| `pwsh -NoProfile -Command (Get-Culture).Name` | Weekday names in the OS locale, once per session, only when `LC_ALL`, `LC_TIME` and `LANG` give no locale, on any OS |
| `node -e <tail reader> <transcript>` | A transcript over 4 MiB |

PitBoard writes no file and changes no setting. It keeps the five-hour readings of the last 3 hours
and the weekly readings of the last 6 hours in the store Claude Code gives each plugin, so a new
session starts with a Pace.

## Requirements

| Requirement | Needed for |
|---|---|
| Claude Code 2.1.287 or later | The row |
| `git` | `Branch` |
| `pwsh` (PowerShell 7) | Weekday names in the OS locale when `LC_ALL`, `LC_TIME` and `LANG` give no locale, on any OS |
| `node` | Cache hits and the TTL from a transcript over 4 MiB |
| [PaceLine](https://agentpit-lab.github.io/agentpit/plugins/paceline/docs/getting-started.html) | Readings other sessions saw, and Pace from the first draw |
| PaceLine's usage-watch | Model-scoped limits |

`git`, `pwsh`, and `node` help only when they are on the `PATH` of the environment Claude Code
starts in ([limitations](limitations.md#some-readings-need-git-pwsh-or-node)). The layout is fixed;
PitBoard has no settings.
